riskTone.label: BEARISH
riskTone.rationale: US-Iran flare-up signals geopolitical risk-off; higher-for-longer rate view adds hawkish headwind, mildly bearish for UK100.

briefing.briefing: Sterling (GBPUSD) fell -0.32% today, which — because UK100 and GBP move in opposite directions — is technically a mild tailwind for the index (cheaper pound boosts the dollar and euro earnings of FTSE multinationals), though the system rates this effect as NEUTRAL given its small size. The dominant forces in play right now are a massive 9.16% surge in Brent crude oil (the price of a barrel of oil), which is strongly bullish for Shell and BP — the two largest energy stocks in the index — while US equity markets (S&P 500 -0.81%, Nasdaq -1.99%) are dragging in the opposite direction, and European peers (Euro Stoxx 50 -0.65%, DAX -0.45%) are also lower, all pointing to a cautious global mood. Gilt yields (the interest rate the UK government pays to borrow money) have eased slightly — the 10-year gilt is down 6 basis points — and crucially there is no long-end gilt stress, so there is no fiscal panic signal to worry about today. The key recent catalyst, flagged by Reuters about 3 hours ago, is a US-Iran geopolitical flare-up: this is pushing oil sharply higher (good for energy stocks) but also spreading a broader risk-off mood (bad for everything else) and reinforcing a 'higher-for-longer' interest rate view that is weighing on gold (-2.94%) and sentiment generally. The overall picture is CHOPPY and finely balanced: energy bulls versus a risk-off Wall Street and European drag, with LOW conviction either way — overall bias scores -2 out of 10, sitting on the mildly bearish side of neutral. Confidence is 4/10; what would change the view is a clear break in oil prices reversing the energy tailwind, or a sharp deterioration in US futures overnight pushing the index decisively lower. For the 08:00 Opening Range Breakout trade: the ORB has already broken DOWN (price broke below the overnight low range), 62% of the 14-day average daily range (133 points) has already been used, leaving roughly 51 points of typical daily movement remaining — this is a fakeout/sweep risk environment rather than a clean trend day, and longs from open need to respect the downside break that has already occurred. On the calendar, there is nothing scheduled for today (Monday), but US CPI (inflation data — the single most watched monthly US number) prints tomorrow Tuesday at 13:30 BST — this is HIGH impact and could sharply move both sterling and the index, so any position held into tomorrow afternoon carries significant news risk; UK GDP data also prints Wednesday 07:00 BST. Key levels: overnight high 10,526, overnight low 10,443, ORB high 10,526, ORB low 10,482, prior day high 10,537 as the ceiling, and prior day low 10,439 as the floor — the index is currently at 10,490, sitting in the middle of the range. Energy is the bull case, geopolitics and Wall Street are the bear case — until one side breaks decisively, wait for confirmation before committing.
